menu.name: Kontrol-ID
menu.tooltiptext: Managed Windows identity and proxy authentication

field.description: Enable identity enforcement after the PKI is created and Windows stations have been enrolled. Installation defaults to disabled to avoid interrupting Internet access.

Client → Squid + Kontrol-ID identity/authentication → E2Guardian ICAP → Internet
Kontrol-ID owns the transport settings while enabled: explicit proxy on 3128 or transparent interception on 3128/3129, and E2Guardian ICAP on 127.0.0.1:1344. Squid is the only TLS interception point and sends the original client IP, resolved username and decrypted URL to E2Guardian. Previous Squid and E2Guardian values are restored when the managed stack is disabled.

Transparent mode identifies the workstation by source IP and does not challenge the browser. Explicit mode requires clients to use the proxy address or PAC/WPAD and supports Kerberos, NTLM and Basic authentication.

option.name: Basic using selected Kontrol authentication server

field.description: DNS name used by explicit proxy clients and by the Kerberos HTTP service principal, for example proxy.example.corp.
DNS domain used for Kerberos/NTLM, for example example.corp. The Kerberos realm is generated in uppercase.
FQDN of the preferred AD controller. DNS and time synchronization must be functional before joining.
Short NetBIOS domain name used by Samba/Winbind, for example EXAMPLE.
Maximum helper processes reserved for explicit proxy authentication.

HTTP-only is the safe onboarding mode. HTTP + HTTPS enables Squid SSL Bump for the selected access mode and automatically selects the internal Kontrol-ID CA. Every inspected client must first be enrolled so the CA is installed in Windows.
Interfaces where Squid listens for explicit clients or where Kontrol-ID installs transparent HTTP/HTTPS redirects.

The package-owned Kontrol-ID Internal CA is selected in Squid automatically and its private key remains on the appliance. The Windows provisioner installs only the public CA certificate in the Trusted Root store.
Enable Squid and install the reversible Kontrol-ID identity/authentication policy for the selected access mode.
Enable E2Guardian ICAP on loopback, disable its independent transparent/MITM rules and send the identified, decrypted Squid requests with their original client IP and username.
Native Windows WinRM HTTPS listener port.
TCP and TLS connection timeout in milliseconds.
Maximum duration of a WinRM identity request in milliseconds.
Require the endpoint certificate to be issued by the selected Kontrol-ID CA.
Require the enrolled hostname to match the endpoint certificate SAN.
Seconds to retain a successful automatic identity.
Seconds before retrying an unknown or unreachable station.
Seconds a previous successful identity may be reused during a temporary endpoint failure.
Lifetime of a manually authenticated IP session in seconds.
Identity returned to Squid when automatic identification is unavailable.
Portal redirects are reliable for HTTP. HTTPS also requires the Kontrol CA/SSL inspection or network captive-portal assistance.
Leave empty to use the Kontrol WebGUI hostname and /kontrol_id_portal.php.
Message shown when the user needs an account or administrative assistance.

Basic authentication and the fallback portal reuse a server from System > User Manager > Authentication Servers without duplicating its credentials. Kerberos and NTLM domain membership are managed separately under Domain and Keytab. The local database remains available for networks without Active Directory.
Select the Kontrol local database or an LDAP/AD authentication server already managed by the base system. Credentials are never copied into the Kontrol-ID package configuration.
Local Kontrol users must belong to this non-administrative group.
Comma-separated AD/LDAP group names. Matching is case-insensitive.
Log endpoint query failures to the system log. Passwords and certificates are never logged.
